earnings.headline: Intuit grew sales 14 percent in its last quarter and full year, but expects slower growth next year.
points: Sales (revenue) for the year rose 14 percent to $21.4 billion. The last quarter also grew 14 percent, to $4.4 billion.
Profit per share (EPS) rose 20 percent to $16.46 for the year. Its newer 'Big Bets' products grew 34 percent.
Their own forecast (guidance) for next year is sales up 9% to 10%, slower than this year's 14 percent.
Weak spots: U.S. TurboTax users fell to 39.0 million from 39.9 million. Mailchimp sales are expected flat to slightly down.
Intuit sells TurboTax (taxes), Credit Karma (credit and loans), QuickBooks (business accounting) and Mailchimp (email marketing).
Credit Karma sales rose 20 percent to $2.6 billion. TurboTax grew more slowly, up 7 percent to $5.3 billion.
It spent $5.5 billion buying back its own stock, up 96 percent. It holds $7.2 billion in cash but owes $7.7 billion in debt.
Risks they name: competition, the government doing taxes itself, keeping up with AI, hacking and fraud, and a restructuring plan.
Several headlines say the stock has been falling, including one drop of 7% before its next earnings report.
One article ties the drop to fears that a new AI finance tool could compete with TurboTax.
The next earnings report is set for November 19.

takeaways: The business grew well last year: sales and profit both rose, and it passed $20 billion in yearly sales.
Growth is expected to slow next year, and fewer people used TurboTax this year than last year.
Investors are worried AI tools could take tax customers away. Intuit says AI is central to its own plan.
